field: # OCR consistently misses Ö for these surnames; frequency-based normalization
# cannot detect the error because the correct form never appears in the data.
# Add new rows here whenever you find another systematic OCR miss.
# DOERING: extra 'E' OCR noise before the missing umlaut
# ── OE → Ö two-letter transcription (no Ö form ever appears in the data) ────
# These names only appear in the OE form; the Ö form never occurs so the
# frequency-based grouping introduced in _strip_umlauts cannot catch them.
# ── OE/AE from extended grouping — rare Dutch name where OE is correct ────
# VERHÖVEN is an OCR/transcription artifact of the Dutch surname VERHOEVEN.
# After the OE→O grouping step VERHOEVEN would be erroneously normalised to
# VERHÖVEN (the umlaut form wins by frequency); this entry corrects that.
# OCR misreads 'J' as 'O' or misses the leading 'J' in JOHANN.
# BÖHME engraved on plate → OCR reads as Cyrillic ВОНМЕ → after Latin substitution: BOHME
